note: TWO whitespace classes for two purposes (R32a''', 2026-10-22, D-SINK-36; R32a'' before it, D-SINK-32, D-SINK-33). `codePoints` is the READER's class: the union of JavaScript's \s (as node and Qt's V4 read it), Python's \s (str.isspace) and U+FEFF, enumerated code point by code point, which the two URL validators REFUSE (Model.validateSourceUrl through Model.isUrlSpaceAt / URL_SPACE_CODES, the helper's validate_source_url through _URL_SPACE over URL_SPACE_CHARS) so that neither engine's own notion is ever consulted. `delimiters` is the REDACTOR's class: the six ASCII whitespace characters, and nothing else, end a free-text URL's RUN and its AUTHORITY in both redactors (Model.redactUrls / runHostParts through Model.isUrlDelimiterAt / URL_DELIMITER_CODES, the helper's redact_urls / run_host_parts through _URL_TAIL_RE and _URL_DELIMITER over URL_DELIMITER_CHARS). A reader refuses, a redactor delimits: under R32a'' both redactors ended the run at the union and each mirror took the other's worse case -- the helper printed the username and the password's tail for U+FEFF where 0.14.3 printed the host (D-SINK-36). Both suites (tests/Model.test.js under 'R32a'''', tests/test_helper.py under the same name) read this file and assert, for EVERY code point of the whole Unicode range, that each mirror's two classes hold exactly these lists; each also asserts its own engine's \s is a proper subset of the union and a proper superset of the delimiters, so a change in either engine is seen rather than absorbed. `'`, `"`, `<` and `>` are in neither on purpose: they ended the helper's run until R32a'' (D-SINK-33) and are trailing punctuation now (tests/fixtures/redaction-vectors.json).

codePoints.name: ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE (the byte-order mark)
